Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are a type of artificial neural network that are used to learn a set of over-complete, latent representations of input data. They are typically used for unsupervised learning and feature learning.

The key property of SAEs is sparsity. During the training process, SAEs are encouraged to produce sparse, or infrequently active, latent representations. This is achieved by adding a penalty term to the cost function that discourages the network from using too many active nodes at the same time.

The network consists of multiple layers of stochastic, latent variables. The first layer is the input layer, where the network receives the data. The last layer is the output layer, where the network produces the reconstructed input data. In between these two layers are one or more layers of stochastic, latent variables.
